JOURNAL

Before a song is finished

2026.09.16

Very few songs get written in a single sitting. Most of the time it starts as one broken fragment of melody, then sits in a folder for weeks, sometimes months, until one day it gets opened again.

A lot happens in between — the chorus gets rewritten three different ways, a whole verse gets deleted and rewritten, a section that was supposed to be a verse ends up becoming the bridge. Plenty of lines that sound effortless were actually rewritten a dozen times before they stuck.

The hardest part usually isn't the writing itself, but deciding "is this enough?" It's easy for a songwriter to always feel a song could be better, but sometimes knowing when to let go and call a song "finished" is its own kind of practice.

So if a song you hear sounds natural and complete, trust that behind it there were probably several versions that almost got given up on.
